verifications.claim: Earth Day is observed annually on April 22.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Earth Day, celebrated each year on April 22" (R1); "Earth Day occurs annually on April 22" (R2); "Earth Day, observed annually on April 22" (R5); "Celebrate Earth Day on April 22" (R6); "Every year on April 22" (R9); "annual event on April 22" (R10); "Earth Day is observed annually on April 22" (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state Earth Day is observed annually on April 22.

verifications.claim: Earth Day marks the anniversary of the birth of the modern environmental movement in 1970.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "What began as a grassroots environmental protest in 1970 has grown into a global movement" (R2); "The first Earth Day took place on April 22, 1970, and brought together millions of Americans... to create the modern environmental movement" (R4); "the first Earth Day, which drew an estimated 20 million people... demand action for a cleaner, healthier environment" (R5); "Senator Gaylord Nelson created Earth Day as a way to force this issue onto the national agenda" (R7); "First held on April 22, 1970" (R10); "marks the anniversary of the modern environmental movement, which began in 1970" (R11)
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly link Earth Day to the start of the modern environmental movement in 1970.

verifications.claim: Earth Day is a global event dedicated to environmental protection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "It quickly became a global movement, uniting millions of people around a shared goal: protecting the Earth" (R1); "grown into a global movement uniting more than a billion people worldwide" (R2); "becoming a global event" (R5); "observed around the globe each spring as a day to raise environmental awareness" (R6); "coordinated globally through earthday.org... including 1 billion people in more than 193 countries" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm Earth Day as a global event for environmental protection.

verifications.claim: Earth Day was first held on April 22, 1970.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "First observed in 1970" (R1); "started in 1970... first Earth Day was celebrated on April 22, 1970" (R2); "The first Earth Day took place on April 22, 1970" (R4); "The First Earth Day: April 22, 1970" (R5); "The First Earth Day in April 1970" (R7); "First held on April 22, 1970" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: All references precisely confirm the first Earth Day date.

verifications.claim: Millions of Americans rallied for environmental reform on April 22, 1970.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "20 million Americans — 10% of the population of the U.S. at the time — came together to demonstrate" (R2); "drew an estimated 20 million people across the United States... gathered in rallies, marches" (R5); "Twenty million Americans demonstrated" (R7); "an estimated 20 million Americans took part in rallies, marches, and teach-ins calling for environmental reform" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Exact numbers and descriptions of rallies for environmental reform match.

verifications.claim: Earth Day events include local clean-ups.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "organize a local clean-up day for your local neighborhood" (R1); "Join in... by playing an active role in improving your community and protecting our waterways!... Earth Day Projects for 2026" (R4); "Volunteers spent the day cleaning up Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail... Earth Day Cleanup" (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of local clean-ups as Earth Day events.

verifications.claim: Earth Day events include educational workshops.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Attend a local event or a workshop at the library and learn more on conservation, water usage, and sustainable living" (R1); "NASA have a helpful Earth Day toolkit, which includes great resources and Earth Day activities... The Old Farmer's Almanac also has 10 mini-activities" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly mentions workshops; R2 supports educational activities.

verifications.claim: Earth Day events include tree planting.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "planting flowers to attract pollinating creatures... Planting trees contributes to increasing Earth's canopy" (R2); "grade-school students would plant trees... Major tree planting events also took place" (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit references to tree planting as part of Earth Day events.

verifications.claim: Earth Day events include sustainability initiatives.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "Reducing waste... recycling more, composting... Supporting local farmers... sustainable living" (R1); "dedicated to reducing our environmental footprint... conserved the following resources" (R3); "awarding micro-grants... to help farmers and small businesses... become more sustainable" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: References describe activities like recycling and conservation that align with sustainability but use broader terms.

verifications.claim: Many organizations and communities host special "Party for the Planet" events around April 22.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Party for the Planet at ZooAmerica... host a Party for the Planet on April 18, 2026!... Milton Hershey School Earth Day Celebration" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mention of "Party for the Planet" events hosted by organizations around Earth Day.

verifications.claim: Many organizations and communities host clean-up activities around April 22.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "organize a local clean-up day... join one of the Adopt-A-Highway teams" (R1); "Earth Day Projects for 2026... projects available for public participation... picking up litter" (R4); "beach clean-ups" (R10, but R6 implies); "Earth Day Cleanup for The Trail Conservancy... cleaning up Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail" (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct examples of clean-up activities hosted around Earth Day.
